title: Opening principle 2: develop your pieces
summary: Knights and bishops out first, one move each, before the queen goes hunting.
body:
In the opening, **time is material**. Each move should bring a new piece into play.

- Develop **knights and bishops** before rooks and queen.
- Move each piece **once** unless there's a concrete reason.
- An early queen gets chased: every attack on it gives your opponent a free developing move.
- Meet a premature queen attack calmly - defend and develop with tempo.

examples.prompt: Black to move. White's queen came out early and hits e5.
examples.explain: Nc6 develops and defends e5. Don't panic-move pawns in front of your king; the queen will have to move again soon.

examples.prompt: Black to move. White threatens Qxf7 mate.
examples.explain: g6 blocks the attack on f7 and kicks the queen next move (Qe7 or Qf6 also defend). Never miss a mate threat against f7/f2.

examples.prompt: White to move. Bring a new piece into the game.
examples.explain: Nf3 develops toward the center and attacks e5. Bc4 is just as natural; both get you closer to castling.
